administered_by: MassHealth, through the Executive Office of Aging & Independence
eligibility_threshold: Massachusetts does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. The Frail Elder Waiver is for people aged 65 and over, or 60 to 64 with a disability, who meet the level of care for a nursing facility but prefer to remain in the community. Applicants must meet clinical eligibility, need waiver services and go on receiving at least one each month, and live in a community setting that meets the federal Community Rule - which does not include assisted living, group homes or rest homes.
asset_limit_single: Not published on the cited page; the requirement is to meet the financial rules for MassHealth Standard in the community, and special financial rules apply to waiver applicants
asset_limit_couple: Not published on the cited page; spousal rules apply
look_back_period: Not published on the cited page; standard MassHealth transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: MassHealth applicants and members can apply for the Frail Elder Waiver at any time - there is no enrolment window. Clinical eligibility is assessed before enrolment, and a participant must keep receiving at least one waiver service each month to stay eligible.
unique_feature: Enrolment is open year-round rather than through a waitlist or registry, and eligibility continues only while the person actually uses the services - so a family that stops using them can lose the waiver even though the person still qualifies clinically.
